# A `PaymentSplit` naming the bank side rather than a receivable split.
#
# The likeliest mistake once a payment can name its splits: the guids are all
# on the transaction and the bank's is the first of them. Nothing else catches
# it — the bank split is in no lot, belongs to no owner and settles nothing —
# so without a check on the account it went into the invoice's lot, leaving
# the money that arrived counted as the money owed.
#
# Named beside a real receivable split, so the refusal is about the one that
# is wrong rather than about the block being empty.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the account the split is on and
# the account the invoice posts to.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
      PaymentSplit "6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8091223344556"
